SAP (also referred to as Sap or sap) is an enterprise resource planning (ERP) software system developed by the German company SAP SE. It is a comprehensive software solution that integrates various business processes and functions within an organization, such as finance, accounting, human resources, supply chain management, and customer relationship management. [1]

The SAP system is widely used by large and medium-sized companies across different industries to streamline their operations, improve efficiency, and make data-driven decisions. It provides a centralized platform for managing and processing various types of business data, including customer information, financial transactions, inventory levels, and production schedules. [2]

Some of the key modules and components of the SAP system include:

1. Financial Accounting (FI): Handles financial transactions, general ledger, accounts payable, and accounts receivable. [2]
2. Controlling (CO): Supports cost accounting, cost center accounting, and profitability analysis. [2]
3. Materials Management (MM): Manages procurement, inventory, and logistics. [2]
4. Sales and Distribution (SD): Handles sales, distribution, and customer relationship management. [2]
5. Human Resources (HR): Manages personnel-related processes such as payroll, time management, and talent management. [2]
6. Industry-specific modules (IS-U, IS-H, etc.): Provide specialized functionality for different industries like utilities, healthcare, and more. [2]
